name: Broken Access Control
what_to_check: Per-object and per-function checks, tenant isolation, CSRF, and SSRF (CWE-918 now sits here).
repo_note: Access control strong and tested; SSRF, now in A01, has no rule anywhere.

name: Security Misconfiguration
what_to_check: Security headers, TLS, public buckets, default settings, verbose errors, XXE, permissive CORS.
repo_note: Free settings plus guard tests keep them on; CORS only warned about, not constrained.

name: Software Supply Chain Failures
what_to_check: Unvetted packages, install scripts, moved tags, unpinned images, compromised CI, vulnerable components.
repo_note: Most complete area in the repo.

name: Cryptographic Failures
what_to_check: TLS versions, encryption at rest, token storage, key management, weak or hand-rolled crypto.
repo_note: Managed TLS at edge, provider keys, hand-rolled crypto banned; no backend TLS rule or key inventory (ASVS V11.1, V12.3).

name: Injection
what_to_check: SQL/NoSQL, OS command, XSS, template and expression injection from any untrusted input.
repo_note: Queries parameterised; no rule on HTML sinks/CSP in web client or on shell/command use.

name: Insecure Design
what_to_check: Threat modelling, abuse cases, secure patterns, file upload design, business-limit design.
repo_note: Design is security-led, but no threat-modelling or abuse-case step is required per feature.

name: Authentication Failures
what_to_check: Credential stuffing, weak passwords, MFA, session fixation, token validation, enumeration.
repo_note: Managed IdP, gateway verification, PKCE; MFA offered not required, no logout/revocation or breached-password rule.

name: Software or Data Integrity Failures
what_to_check: Unsigned updates, unpinned CI inputs, unsafe deserialization, mass assignment, unverified webhooks.
repo_note: Pinned inputs, deploy-time generation, dedicated request types, webhook signatures checked first.

name: Security Logging and Alerting Failures
what_to_check: Security events logged, tamper-resistant audit, alerts on attack patterns, no secrets in logs.
repo_note: Errors well reported; no security-event log (sign-in, role change) and no alerting on attacks.

name: Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions
what_to_check: Fail closed, no swallowed errors, no detail in error responses, consistent error handling.
repo_note: Strongest area: one root handler, request id only, generation fails closed.

name: Broken Object Level Authorization
what_to_check: Swap object IDs across users, branches and tenants on every read and write endpoint.
repo_note: Ownership check is a required step; isolation fixtures cover branches, not per-user ownership.

name: Broken Authentication
what_to_check: Token validation, issuer/audience, refresh handling, brute force on sign-in and recovery.
repo_note: Gateway verifies tokens; brute-force and refresh-token rotation left to provider defaults, not mandated.

name: Broken Object Property Level Authorization
what_to_check: Responses leak fields to lower roles; requests set fields the caller may not (mass assignment).
repo_note: Separate response type per role; dedicated request type per endpoint; privacy flag required.

name: Unrestricted Resource Consumption
what_to_check: Rate limits, body size, page size caps, upload size, cost-driving calls, spend alerts.
repo_note: No per-user/tenant quota or maximum page size; body limit stated for tool server only.

name: Broken Function Level Authorization
what_to_check: Call admin or other-role endpoints directly; empty or stale role lists.
repo_note: Explicit anonymous role, route table generated at deploy, tests both ways.

name: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
what_to_check: Automated abuse of sign-up, invites, submissions, purchases; bot defence per flow.
repo_note: Public endpoints rate-limited and no open sign-up; no per-flow abuse analysis for authenticated flows.

name: Server Side Request Forgery
what_to_check: Any server fetch of a caller-supplied URL: imports, webhooks, link previews, avatars.
repo_note: No rule on outbound fetches, URL allowlists or blocking metadata/internal addresses.

name: Security Misconfiguration
what_to_check: Headers, TLS, CORS, error verbosity, unpatched components, default configs.

name: Improper Inventory Management
what_to_check: Unknown endpoints, old versions, exposed non-prod hosts, undocumented tool surface.
repo_note: Routes generated from code and tool list pinned; no rule on retiring old hosts or exposing staging.

name: Unsafe Consumption of APIs
what_to_check: Trusting third-party responses, webhooks, inbound mail without validation or limits.
repo_note: Third-party payloads treated as untrusted; no timeouts, size caps or TLS rules for outbound calls.

name: Prompt Injection
what_to_check: Untrusted data returned by tools (user-authored text) steering the agent into harmful calls.
repo_note: Blast radius limited by no-privilege server and allowlist; tool output is not marked as untrusted data.

name: Sensitive Information Disclosure
what_to_check: Personal data or secrets reaching model context through tool results or errors.
repo_note: Personal-data endpoints never on allowlist; redacting derived tools; no secrets in results.

name: Excessive Agency
what_to_check: Tools with more permission, functionality or autonomy than needed; irreversible actions.
repo_note: User's own token, default-off allowlist, irreversible/legal acts kept off, no standing privilege.

name: Supply Chain
what_to_check: Compromised packages in the tool server; third-party models, adapters or datasets.
repo_note: Package side covered; the architecture uses no third-party model or dataset.

name: Data and Model Poisoning
what_to_check: Poisoned training, fine-tuning or retrieval data altering model behaviour.
repo_note: The architecture trains, fine-tunes and hosts no model; it only serves tools.

name: Unbounded Consumption
what_to_check: Large tool results, huge bodies, loops of calls running up cost or context.
repo_note: Results capped, 413 before validation, staged-payload cost ceilings, spend alerts.

name: Misinformation
what_to_check: Model misreading tool results: wrong tenant, partial counts, unfinished jobs.
repo_note: Results name tenant, surface dropped counts, poll to terminal state; model accuracy otherwise out of scope.

name: Hidden Context Exposure
what_to_check: Hidden context (system prompts, tool schemas, instructions) exposing secrets or authz logic.
repo_note: Replaces System Prompt Leakage. App owns no prompt; tool schemas are public by design. Gist unverified.

name: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
what_to_check: Cross-tenant leakage or poisoning through a shared vector store / RAG index.
repo_note: No vector store or RAG in the architecture.

name: Improper Output Handling
what_to_check: Model-generated tool arguments passed to queries, HTML or shell without validation.
repo_note: Tool calls hit the same API: shape check, use-case validation, parameterised queries.

name: Agent Goal Hijack
what_to_check: Content in tool results redirecting the agent toward other tenants' data or destructive calls.
repo_note: App cannot stop hijack; it bounds what a hijacked agent can do via the user's token.

name: Tool Misuse
what_to_check: Legitimate tools chained or called with harmful arguments; tools usable beyond intent.
repo_note: Default-off allowlist enforced in API; derived tools enforce safe call order.

name: Identity & Privilege Abuse
what_to_check: Agent tokens over-scoped, reused across resources, stored in clear, or carrying standing privilege.
repo_note: Resource-bound tokens, hashed, CMK, TTL; server holds no data access; consent every time.

name: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
what_to_check: Compromised MCP SDK, tool definitions or registered clients at runtime.
repo_note: Tools built from manifest; clients by redirect allowlist; packages under 28.

name: Unexpected Code Execution
what_to_check: Agent-generated input reaching eval, shell or code-execution tools.
repo_note: Tools are generated RPC endpoints; no tool executes code or shell.

name: Memory & Context Poisoning
what_to_check: Persisted agent state (active tenant, staged bodies) corrupted to steer later calls.
repo_note: Stored tenant grants nothing and is named in results; agent-side memory out of scope.

name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
what_to_check: Forged or unauthenticated messages between cooperating agents.
repo_note: No agent-to-agent channel in the architecture.

name: Cascading Failures
what_to_check: One failing call amplified through retries, loops or downstream jobs.
repo_note: Retry caps and poll timeouts; no circuit breaker or per-agent call budget.

name: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
what_to_check: User approves harmful action because agent or client misrepresents it.
repo_note: Consent shows real client name, host, account; no in-flow confirmation for high-impact tool calls.

name: Rogue Agents
what_to_check: Agent acting outside intent with no detection, audit or kill switch.
repo_note: Revoke and allowlist exist; no per-agent audit trail or anomaly alerting.
